learning_outcomes.text: Critically reflect on the nature of science and technology, and on the broader role of science and technology in modern society.
Have knowledge and understanding of the various discussed problems, positions, and arguments.
Be able to sharply distinguish and critically confront different positions and arguments.
Be able to apply the acquired insights to more concrete action situations where the studied philosophical theories and arguments may be relevant.

syllabus_topics: The inherent nature of science and technology: How scientific knowledge differs from other forms of knowledge?
What is typical about scientific rationality?
How certain are we of the insights science provides?
What is the role of observation and experimentation?
What is the role of theory formation?
What is the relationship between science and technology?
Science and technology within the broader framework of modernity.
The relationship between science and technology and other societal domains such as morality, politics, or economy.
How moral rationality differs from scientific rationality?
Does technology determine our economic development?
What is the relationship between democracy and technocracy in a globalized world?
Can a high-tech and rationalized society lead to alienation and loss of meaning?

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (multiple-choice with correction for guessing)

assessment_rules: The examination is a two-hour multiple-choice exam with correction for guessing. More detailed explanations about the exam format and grading method will be provided during lectures and via PowerPoint (available on Toledo).
bibliography: Stefan Rummens, "Filosofie. Een thematische inleiding", Lannoo Campus, 2024
